newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-KUERTEN BEATS MEDVEDEV IN TWO-DAY FRENCH OPEN MARATHON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KUERTEN BEATS MEDVEDEV IN TWO-DAY FRENCH OPEN MARATHON.

text.p: Gustavo Kuerten finished off a tense two-day duel with Andrei Medvedev on Monday to become the first Brazilian in 29 years to reach the quarter-finals of the French Open.

Medvedev, playing his best tennis since he last made an appearance in the quarter-finals at Roland Garros in 1994, refused to go easily and extended the colourful Brazilian, kitted out from head-to-toe in blue and yellow, to five sets 5-7 6-1 6-2 1-6 7-5.
Kuerten, who dispatched 1995 champion Thomas Muster in the third round, next faces last year's champion Yevgeny Kafelnikov aiming to become the first Brazilian to reach the semifinals.
The match resumed on Monday with the players level at two sets and two games each after darkness had descended on Roland Garros and forced an end to a cold, windswept day's play on Sunday.

Showing no sign of the nerves which could have festered overnight, Kuerten, ranked 66 in the world, picked up where he left off, holding his serve and then breaking Medvedev to wrest control of the set 4-2.
But suddenly, with an historic victory in sight, Kuerten looked as if he would fold under the pressure as Medvedev broke back, held serve and had the young Brazilian down 0-40, ready to break again.
But Kuerten fought back to force deuce then blasted a pair of aces past the Ukrainian to hold his serve.
The scare seemed to calm Kuerten, who immediately put the pressure on Medvedev.

The Brazilian piled up three match points before converting his fourth opportunity, breaking Medvedev with a well-placed lob to become the first Brazilian to reach the quarter-finals at Roland Garros since Tomas Koch in 1968.
"It's the best week in my life," smiled the 20-year-old Kuerten as he left the court. "I feel so good on court, every shot I try, I make.
"I had four match points and the first three I should have finished easily but with the fourth I was lucky to make this lob."
